success_patterns: Verbatim archive hits (J! Archive, GitHub jeopardy dumps, StudyStack all-caps flashcards, TriviaBistro) gave the answer directly. The agents copied it in the archive's own form: 'Pippi' completed to 'Pippi Longstocking' from other passages, 'Clifford Odets', 'hand dryer', 'pudding'.

When there was no archive line, the agents picked the entity repeated across many passage titles and snippets that matched the clue's anchors: Georgia for Brasstown Bald, John Fogerty for 'Proud Mary', Abdullah for 'servant of Allah'.

The agents resolved the direction of a nickname clue. 'William Marcy Tweed's better known moniker' asks for the nickname itself, so the answer was the bare 'Boss', not 'Boss Tweed' or the real name. This is the reverse of the existing rule for clues that give the nickname.
The agents gave bare answers with no category words or clue echoes: 'pudding' for 'hasty', 'Boss', and 'Georgia' without any added descriptor.

patch.reasoning: Most successes were already covered by the verbatim-hit, truncation, delete-clue-words and referent rules. The one uncovered pattern is nickname direction. The existing rule only says to answer the real name when the clue gives a nickname. In the Tweed trajectory the clue gave the real name and asked for the moniker, and the correct answer was the bare nickname. Without an explicit two-way rule, an agent could over-apply the existing rule and answer 'William Tweed'.

edits.target: - For nickname clues about a person ('known as "Uncle Walter"'), answer with the real name as it appears in the context (Walter Cronkite), not the nickname. Still apply the person-name rule above.
edits.content: - Nickname clues about a person work in BOTH directions, so check which one is given. If the clue gives the nickname ('known as "Uncle Walter"'), answer with the real name as it appears in the context (Walter Cronkite), not the nickname. If the clue gives the real name and asks for the 'better known moniker / nickname / alias / stage name' ('William Marcy Tweed's better known moniker'), answer with the nickname alone ('Boss'), not the real name and not the nickname plus surname ('Boss Tweed'). Still apply the person-name rule above.
